section_summary: The section closes a proposal to extend Japanese fishing grounds north and northeast of Hokkaido, followed by State Department discussion of the proposal and concern about Soviet influence among fishermen. It also documents Chinese seizures of Japanese fishing vessels, including diplomatic protests and a fisherman's sworn account. Later papers concern Japanese fisheries policy, Canadian port privileges, consultation with industry advisers, Antarctic whaling, and a separate 1947 note about pearl imports.

subfiles.title: Proposed northern extension of the Japanese fishing area: analysis and recommendation
subfiles.about: Recommends proposing an enlarged fishing area north of Hokkaido and inviting Soviet comment.
subfiles.summary: The analysis argues that the existing limits waste fuel, create navigational hazards, hamper production, and encourage violations. It estimates a substantial increase in catch from an extension. It also urges placing on record that the northern fishing limit is not a permanent political boundary and publishing any Soviet objection.

subfiles.title: Draft letter to the Soviet member of the Allied Council for Japan
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Soviet member of the Allied Council for Japan
subfiles.about: Notifies the Soviet representative of proposed coordinates for an expanded Japanese fishing area.
subfiles.summary: Cites production, economic hardship, and navigation near Hokkaido, and invites Soviet comment on the proposed boundary.

subfiles.title: Draft note for record on northern fishing boundary
subfiles.about: Records the grounds for referring the proposed northern boundary change to the Soviet representative.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes earlier boundary orders, expected benefits, Soviet consultation, and offices asked to concur.

subfiles.title: Check sheet on extension of the northern boundary of the authorized fishing area
subfiles.about: Advises holding the northern extension pending State Department views.
subfiles.summary: Supports recording that the boundary is not permanent, while seeking Washington's position before proceeding.

subfiles.title: Department reply on northern fishing area extension
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Approves the proposed northward extension in principle and asks to review a negative Soviet reply before publication.
subfiles.summary: The Department treats fishing boundaries as within SCAP's executive authority and recalls its position that no Far Eastern Commission policy was needed.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo despatch 759
subfiles.about: Recommends a reply supporting the Hokkaido fishing extension while clarifying SCAP's authority.
subfiles.summary: Reviews expected catch gains, hazardous narrow passages, and the Soviet consultation proposal. It recommends Department concurrence, review of any negative Soviet response before publication, and clarification that SCAP need not await Far Eastern Commission action.

subfiles.title: Departure of fourth Antarctic whaling expedition
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese ships departing for the fourth postwar Antarctic whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Notes SCAP approval, planned departures of two fleets, and the absence of known protests against the quieter authorization procedure.

subfiles.title: Communist activity concerning northern fisheries
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports a Communist-backed conference advocating renewed northern fishing through Japan–Soviet friendship.
subfiles.summary: The airgram describes press accounts of the conference and activity in Hakodate, suggesting the Soviet Union could use northern fishing rights in peace negotiations.

subfiles.title: Seizures of Japanese fishing vessels by Chinese patrols
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports protests over Chinese seizure, detention, and alleged military use of Japanese fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: The despatch reports 33 vessels seized, two sunk, ten deaths, and many crews detained. Sebald describes evidence that Chinese forces armed captured vessels and used them to seize others. He recounts his meeting with General Chu, requests return and compensation, and doubts a quick resolution amid China's military crisis.

subfiles.title: Chinese Mission reply concerning four Nitto Maru vessels
subfiles.about: Explains the seizure of four Japanese fishing boats and denies their military use.
subfiles.summary: Claims the boats fished outside SCAP limits, promises crew repatriation, and rejects allegations that seized vessels were armed.

subfiles.title: Diplomatic Section protest listing additional Chinese seizures
subfiles.about: Protests additional seizures and seeks the return of vessels and crews.
subfiles.summary: Lists Japanese fishing vessels reportedly attacked, sunk, or confiscated by Chinese forces, including craft allegedly recaptured by armed former Japanese boats. It requests their release, the crews' return, and a full account of each incident.

subfiles.title: Aide-mémoire on Chinese seizure and military use of Japanese vessels
subfiles.to: Lieutenant General Chu Shih-ming, Chinese Mission in Japan
subfiles.about: Presents evidence that Chinese forces armed captured Japanese boats and demands remedial action.
subfiles.summary: Sebald cites a fisherman's affidavit identifying armed former Japanese fishing boats used as Chinese patrol craft. He challenges China's asserted authority to seize Japanese vessels on the high seas and asks for an end to seizures, release of vessels and crews, and compensation for losses.

subfiles.title: Sworn statement by Tadao Hashimoto
subfiles.about: Describes the armed capture of the Akashi Maru No. 99 and identifies seized Japanese boats in Chinese hands.
subfiles.summary: Hashimoto recounts machine-gun fire, detention, transfer through Dinghai and Keelung, and repair work on seized boats. He identifies former Japanese vessels used as armed Chinese craft and lists others he saw in port.

subfiles.title: Return of letters for corrections
subfiles.about: Returns confidential fisheries letters for packaging, wording, filing, and clearance corrections.
subfiles.summary: Requests marked envelopes, a wording change, a file memorandum, and BNA clearance.

subfiles.title: Follow-up on confidential letters
subfiles.to: Mr. Dak, BNA; Miss Daniels, S/S-CR
subfiles.about: Confirms that suggested corrections to the confidential letters were made.
subfiles.summary: Notes an attached memorandum and offers clarification to the recipients.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Japanese fishing areas and Canadian port privileges
subfiles.about: Records discussion with Dr. Chapman about fishing-area expansion and reciprocal port access with Canada.
subfiles.summary: Participants consider inspection arrangements, the Philippines boundary question, high-seas freedom, conservation, and benefits for trust territories. They also discuss whether Canadian vessels should receive privileges at U.S. Pacific ports south of Seattle and await a fuller statement of Customs objections.

subfiles.title: Consultation with West Coast fishery advisers on Japan peace treaty
subfiles.about: Confirms approval to show selected industry advisers draft fisheries treaty language.
subfiles.summary: Fearey and Dulin accept disclosure of the article's wording, provided negotiation timing remains confidential.

subfiles.title: Letter to Miller Freeman and distribution list for identical letters
subfiles.from: W. M. Chapman, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Miller Freeman and other fisheries advisory committee members
subfiles.about: Sends a confidential SCAP despatch on Japanese fisheries to industry advisers.
subfiles.summary: The letter links SCAP's discussions to a proposed Pacific Ocean Fisheries Convention among the United States, Canada, and Japan. It instructs recipients to handle the enclosed despatch confidentially; the following page lists nine recipients of identical letters.

subfiles.title: Clearance note on transmitting confidential fisheries material
subfiles.about: Requests verification of arrangements for sending confidential material to industry representatives.
subfiles.summary: Notes conditional initialing of the letter and suggests Canadian desk clearance.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on stimulating Japanese pearl imports
subfiles.from: Assistant Secretary of State, signature unclear
subfiles.about: Requests action on an Imperial Pearl Syndicate proposal concerning pearl imports from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Asks Claxton to consult Petersen and USCC personnel and draft a reply for General Hilldring.
